inspection.surface: six-view textured orbit renders of each completed TRELLIS cast
inspection.basis: direct visual inspection after canonical Greenroom completion

claimAxes.macrostructure: Whether TRELLIS produced one coherent animal volume with the expected head, trunk, supports, and tail.
claimAxes.supportSeparation: Whether the four supports remain visually distinct enough to seed correspondence or fitting.
claimAxes.backsideCompletion: Whether unseen geometry closes coherently rather than collapsing, duplicating, or fusing major structures.
claimAxes.surfaceGeometry: Whether local geometry is smooth and stable enough to carry deformation, independent of semantic recognizability.
claimAxes.reuseDisposition: candidate means plausible deformation substrate; conditional means useful after repair or surface replacement; appearance-only means retain visual semantics but reject the generated surface as the deformation carrier; control means intentionally diagnostic rather than reusable.

neutral-seed80301.note: Recognizable complete animal and preserved body organization; rough shard-like surface and belly/support artifacts require surface replacement or substantial repair.

neutral-seed80302.note: Canid-like cast remains structurally readable, but visible fur transitions become unstable geometric facets.

neutral-seed80413.note: Cleanest neutral reconstruction; macrostructure is strong with localized facial fringe and minor surface repair still required.

skin-seed80301.note: Clean closed animal volume with plausible smooth surface; a localized doubled or ambiguous rear support remains the main correspondence risk.

skin-seed80302.note: Coherent smooth cast from all inspected views; paws and face are prior-driven, but all four supports and the global body organization survive.

skin-seed80413.note: Strong smooth reconstruction with clean tail and separated supports; local facial and foot details are generator-specific but do not compromise the carrier volume.

short-fur-seed80301.note: Head, ears, trunk, supports, and rear volume survive, but millions of fur-derived geometric shards destroy stable local correspondence.

short-fur-seed80302.note: Better paws, muzzle, tail, and whole-body completion than the first fur seed, but high-relief coat geometry still makes the cast unsuitable as the primary deformation surface.

short-fur-seed80413.note: Third independent recurrence of fur-derived shard geometry; the body, head, and supports survive, but the tail is weak and the generated coat is unsuitable for local correspondence.

armor-seed80301.note: Broad plates survive as spatially distinct riding components across the back, shoulders, hips, and limbs while a continuous organism remains visible underneath.

armor-seed80302.note: Strongest rigid-component reconstruction: overlapping back, hip, chest, and limb plates remain visibly layered around a continuous body with unusually clean separation.

armor-seed80413.note: Heavier armor basin still reconstructs coherent riding plates over the torso and supports; borders need cleanup, but the rigid/underbody distinction remains strong.

shell-seed80301.note: TRELLIS faithfully reconstructs the FLUX collapse as a smooth closed shell object; this is a clean negative control showing that reconstruction cannot recover organism structure erased upstream.

shell-seed80302.note: TRELLIS preserves the weak organism that survived FLUX, but the shell remains an enormous dominant body volume and the supports are subordinate damaged appendages.

shell-seed80413.note: Second complete upstream collapse reconstructed faithfully as a smooth helmet-like shell with a rim and rear loop; no organism structure is recoverable.

mossy-stone-seed80301.note: The animal and all four supports survive, but pervasive moss detail becomes dense geometric faceting; retain the appearance semantics while replacing the deformation surface.

mossy-stone-seed80302.note: Coherent stone regions and animal supports survive, but leaf-like moss relief covers most of the body; useful for material-region inference, not as the primary deformation mesh.

mossy-stone-seed80413.note: Cleanest mossy-stone cast: the stone body is comparatively smooth and all four supports survive, but moss still creates patchy relief and the tail is weak; retain as an appearance and material-region reference.
